The test image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, dark spots/pustules densely scattered across the surface, with significant yellowing and browning. This is a **leaf** disease.

Top candidates from leaf classes: Southern_Rust, Common_Rust, Tar_Spot, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Southern rust reference shows small orange pustules, less dense than the test image. Let me check Common_Rust.
Common rust shows distinct reddish-brown oval pustules. The test image spots look darker and smaller. Let me check Tar_Spot.
Tar spot shows black raised spots on mostly green leaf. Test image has much more tissue damage. Let me check Physoderma_Brown_Spot.
Physoderma Brown Spot shows small spots in bands with dark midrib spots - similar pattern to the test image! Let me check more candidates. Let me view Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight next.
SCLB shows rectangular lesions, not matching. Let me check Eyespot.
Eyespot shows distinct circular spots with ring patterns - not matching the dense dark spots in the test image. Let me check Holcus_Spot.
Holcus spot is completely different. Let me use my final view to confirm Physoderma_Brown_Spot with another reference.

This second Physoderma Brown Spot reference is an excellent match to the test image. Both show:
- Numerous small spots densely scattered across the leaf in bands
- Dark purplish-black spots concentrated on/near the midrib
- Yellowing and browning of leaf tissue between spots
- Progressive coalescence and darkening of lesions

The test image appears to be a more advanced/severe case of the same disease pattern.
